subject: Intermittent post-deploy control-plane flaps — mitigation & evidence
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Heathaven: control-plane flaps after weekend private deploy

Hi team,

Heathaven reported intermittent control-plane disconnects on their private VPC since our deploy last night (approx 02:30 UTC). They see several 10-30s 'controlplane unreachable' events across their regions, which correlate with increased disk I/O during their nightly backups.

Customer: Heathaven Health (Ben Harris).
Impact: App-level errors for a subset of inference requests; no data loss reported.
Timeline: 02:30 UTC deploy -> first alerts 03:05 UTC -> repeated flaps through the morning.

Action needed: Aditya, can you prioritize an initial triage and gather the following artifacts so we can share with the customer: controlplane heartbeat logs, kube events around 02:00-06:00 UTC, and the deploy manifest diff. Please note any config changes that could affect keepalive/heartbeat behavior.

I'll get a bridge scheduled for 14:00 their local time (16:00 UTC) once we have a recommended mitigation. Laura, please stand by for customer comms and any short-term credits conversation — they mentioned SLA impact.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: none yet]
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Heathaven: control-plane flaps after weekend private deploy

On Thu, 14 Aug 2025 at 09:12 Mina Haddad wrote:
> Heathaven reported intermittent control-plane disconnects on their private VPC since our deploy last night...

Quick triage summary:
- Root cause hypothesis: the new control-plane binary we rolled out updated the gRPC ping/keepalive thresholds and reduced the default retransmit tolerance. Under high disk I/O (their nightly backups) we observe transient GC pauses and network scheduling jitter; combined, the new thresholds caused short-lived connection terminations.
- Evidence collected: controlplane-heartbeat-log.txt (attached), kube-events-20250814.txt (attached). I captured the 5-minute window with repeated 10-30s disconnects; timestamps line up with their backup job.
- Temporary mitigation: 1) revert the keepalive tuning to previous values, or 2) enable the routing fallback to a standby controlplane binary that tolerates longer timeouts. Both are low-risk and reversible.

Proposed next steps for customer comms: share the logs, recommend immediate enablement of fallback routing while we push a hotfix to restore keepalive defaults. I'll prepare the manifest patch (privnet-deploy-manifest.patch) to revert the tuning.

Attaching: controlplane-heartbeat-log.txt, kube-events-20250814.txt, privnet-deploy-manifest.patch

Aditya
Aditya Rao
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Harris <ben.harris@heathaven.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent post-deploy control-plane flaps — mitigation & evidence

Hi Ben,

Thanks for raising this — and sorry for the disruption. We dug into the deploy artifacts and have initial findings we want to share before the bridge. Short summary up front: we observed that a control-plane tuning change in last night's private deploy reduced the tolerance for transient network/disk pauses. When Heathaven's nightly backup spikes I/O, the combination produced short control-plane connection terminations.

What we've done so far (immediate):
- Prepared a rollback patch that restores the previous keepalive/retry settings (attached).
- Recommended a quick routing fallback configuration to maintain request routing while we roll the patch (we can apply this in under 15 minutes).
- Collected logs and events for transparency: controlplane-heartbeat-log.txt, kube-events-20250814.txt. Links: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/privnet-logs-HEATHAVEN-20250814

Request: would you be available for a short bridge at 16:00 UTC today so we can walk through the mitigation and, with your approval, perform the fallback then the rollback? If that window doesn't work, propose a window and we'll adjust.

We aim to keep the change low-risk and reversible; the manifest patch is attached as 'privnet-deploy-manifest.patch' and a one-page runbook is attached as 'runbook_redwood_patch.pdf'.

Again, apologies — we'll follow up with a formal post-incident summary once we complete the rollback and confirm stability.

Best,
Mina
Senior Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachments: controlplane-heartbeat-log.txt, kube-events-20250814.txt, privnet-deploy-manifest.patch, runbook_redwood_patch.pdf]

We did see the same gaps in our logs; attaching a short excerpt from our side (their internal scheduler correlated to the times you noted). From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Harris <ben.harris@heathaven.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: control-plane keepalive regression and remediation

Hi Ben (and team),

Thanks again for partnering through the rollback yesterday. This message is a concise post-incident follow-up and next steps.

Summary of findings:
- Root cause: a tuning change in the control-plane binary reduced gRPC keepalive/retry windows. Under elevated disk I/O the process experienced transient pauses that our updated settings interpreted as connection failures.
- Impact: multiple ~10-30s control-plane flaps across your private VPC during nightly backup windows. Some inference requests retried or failed; no data corruption observed.
- Evidence: controlplane-heartbeat-log.txt, kube-events-20250814.txt, plus your scheduler excerpt (thank you). All artifacts are in the shared folder: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/privnet-logs-HEATHAVEN-20250814

What we changed and why:
- Immediate mitigation: enabled routing fallback at 18:00 UTC to reduce surface area for client errors.
- Rollback: applied manifest patch to restore keepalive defaults. Verified stability for 24 hours post-change.

Permanent remediation plan (timeline):
- INF-2148: revert patch in the canary build and add a regression test that simulates I/O-induced scheduling jitter (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Add an automated workload test for private deployments that includes a backup-like I/O pattern to detect regressions before canary (ETA: 4 weeks).
- Documentation: we've updated our private deploy runbook and attached the operation playbook for your team.

Request for closure: please confirm when you'd like us to close this incident; we can remain available for an on-demand review with your SREs. We'll also schedule a short postmortem call next week to walk technical details if desired (proposed: Tue Aug 19, 10:00 UTC).

Apologies again for the disruption. If you want any compensation noted for SLA impact, Laura is looped for follow-up.

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachments: runbook_redwood_patch.pdf]
